pages.title: About
pages.content:
Founded in 2011 by Orla Brennan, Kantei Valuers provides calm, independent commercial property valuations across Ireland from our office in Dublin. We believe in reading the building thoroughly before we read the market, assigning one valuer to see each instruction through from site hour to signature.

Founding Story and Valuation Philosophy

Kantei Valuers was founded in 2011 by Orla Brennan at 27 Merchants Row, Dublin 2. Having previously worked as a panel valuer for a commercial loan book, Orla observed how often property valuations were detached from the physical reality of the building. She established the practice on a clear, disciplined principle: one qualified valuer takes personal responsibility for each instruction from the site hour to the final signature. We value commercial buildings within 150 km of Dublin without travel charges. Every assessment begins with careful physical observation, ensuring our market values are rooted in verified dimensions, visible condition, and factual lease terms rather than distant desk assumptions.

Our Team and Daily Practice

Our team consists of nine people in total, including seven colleagues whom clients and property owners regularly work with. Orla Brennan serves as founder and principal valuer focusing on shops and high-street retail units. Kwame Asante values offices and mixed-use blocks, while Inès Moreau inspects industrial units and warehouses. Tobias Reinholt reads every lease, rent roll, and break clause. Priya Nair maintains our transaction comparables file, and Daniel Kowalczyk reviews each report before signature. Aoife Gallagher manages our instructions desk. A typical day runs from the first site hour at 08:00, further inspections or desk work at 11:00, lease reading and evidence analysis at 14:00, Daniel's final report review at 16:30, before our desk closes at 17:30.

Lender Desk and Owner Desk

To maintain clear lines of responsibility, our instructions are coordinated across two dedicated desks. At our lender desk, Kwame Asante and Orla Brennan handle valuations for banks and commercial lenders requiring loan security assessments for purchases, refinances, and loan reviews, delivering reports in required lender formats. At our owner desk, Inès Moreau and Orla Brennan work directly with property owners, purchasers, and landlords on valuations for sales, acquisitions, lease renewals, rent reviews, and company accounts. Aoife Gallagher coordinates both desks from our Dublin office, issuing fixed written fee quotes within one working day and booking site hours between 08:00 and 16:00 on weekdays.

Recent Instructions Across Ireland

Our practice undertakes commercial valuations across Ireland. Recent instructions illustrate our methodical approach across different asset classes. In Drogheda, we completed a lender instruction for a refinance on a corner shop with a flat above, where examining the lease plan revealed an overlooked let rear yard, with the signed report delivered in eight working days. In Kilkenny, an owner instructed us prior to a sale of a two-storey office building, where we measured two separate floors to net internal area and valued the let and vacant space individually. In Naas, we provided a lease renewal opinion for a warehouse landlord, analyzing five comparable lettings within twenty kilometres.

pages.title: Instructions
pages.content:
Kantei Valuers accepts lender instructions and owner instructions for commercial property across Ireland, providing signed valuation reports within ten working days of the site hour. We provide fixed written fee quotes within one working day of your request.

Lender Instructions

We act for commercial lenders and financial institutions requiring independent market valuations of commercial property offered as loan security. Instructions cover new property purchases, refinancing facilities, and scheduled loan reviews. Every lender instruction is carried out to provide an objective, signed figure that financial underwriters can rely on when making credit decisions. We prepare reports in the lender's required format whenever requested, ensuring all specific covenants, lease terms, and risk disclosures are presented in the lender's preferred structure. While the borrower or property owner typically pays the valuation fee, our professional duty of care remains strictly with the instructing lender.

Owner and Seller Instructions

Property owners, prospective buyers, landlords, and corporate tenants instruct us directly when they require an authoritative valuation for strategic decisions. We value commercial assets ahead of open-market sales or proposed acquisitions, providing clear evidence of current market values and investment yields. Our valuers also provide formal opinions for lease renewals and contested rent reviews, as well as balance-sheet valuations required for annual company accounts. Every owner instruction includes a full sixty-minute site inspection and a signed report explaining recent comparable market transactions, local supply dynamics, and lease covenant strengths so that owners can negotiate or report figures with complete clarity.

Properties We Value and Property Exclusions

Our practice focuses exclusively on commercial real estate. We value five property types: shops and high-street retail units; office buildings and single office floors; industrial units and storage warehouses; mixed-use blocks comprising ground-floor commercial space with residential flats or offices above; and small hotels and leisure buildings. Conversely, there are four categories we do not value under any circumstances: private residential homes; development land without granted planning permission; petrol stations and specialist trading properties; and any buildings located outside Ireland. By concentrating entirely on core commercial buildings within our geographic expertise, we maintain rigorous precision and reliable comparables for every signed valuation.

Required Documents for Instruction

To deliver an accurate valuation within ten working days of the site hour, we require access to core property documents. Instructing parties should provide these records prior to or during our physical inspection. The essential documents include copies of all occupational leases and any supplementary side letters; a current certified rent roll; the registered title plan showing legal boundaries; the past year's service-charge budget and accounts; the current building insurance schedule; and copies of any relevant planning permissions or certificates of compliance. Tobias Reinholt examines every lease clause, rent review provision, and break date to ensure our valuation accurately reflects the legal tenure.

Questions we are asked

Can the borrower instruct?

In commercial lending, the instruction must be issued or formally authorised by the lending institution, even if the borrower is paying the fee. If you are a borrower seeking a refinance or purchase loan, ask your lender to instruct Kantei Valuers directly or provide us with their formal instruction letter. We can liaise with your lender's security team to confirm reporting requirements and issue our written fee quote. This ensures that the signed valuation report addresses the lender directly and meets all internal credit committee criteria without requiring costly re-issuance or delays to your loan facility.

Do you value homes?

No. Kantei Valuers does not value private residential homes, individual apartments, or residential housing schemes. Our practice is dedicated entirely to commercial property valuation. The only residential space we inspect is where flats form an integral part of a mixed-use commercial block, such as an upper-floor apartment situated above a ground-floor retail shop or restaurant. For purely domestic properties, standalone houses, or residential developments, clients must engage an estate agent or residential valuer specializing in the domestic housing market.

How far do you travel?

Our standard practice covers properties situated within 150 kilometres of our Dublin office at 27 Merchants Row, Dublin 2, with no additional travel charges. This operational radius encompasses Leinster and surrounding commercial hubs, including Dublin, Drogheda, Dundalk, Naas, and Kilkenny. For commercial properties situated further across Ireland beyond the 150-kilometre boundary, we are pleased to review the instruction and provide a customized written fee quote that includes any necessary travel time. Aoife Gallagher confirms all travel details in your initial fixed quote.

What if the lender has its own format?

Many financial lenders maintain standardized valuation templates, specific risk matrices, and particular reporting formats for their commercial loan books. Kantei Valuers regularly completes valuations in the lender's designated reporting format whenever requested. Founder Orla Brennan spent years as a panel valuer for commercial loan portfolios and designed our analytical systems to accommodate varied lender frameworks seamlessly. Simply notify us of your lender's format requirements when requesting the appraisal, and Daniel Kowalczyk will ensure our signed twenty-page report and appendices fully satisfy their compliance specifications.

Can we be at the site hour?

Yes, we strongly encourage the property owner, building manager, or letting agent to attend the site hour. Having someone on site who knows the building allows us to examine the lease plan together during the first ten minutes, confirm physical boundaries, and access locked service risers, basements, and roof areas. You can also walk us through any recent tenant fit-outs, maintenance works, or historical issues. If an owner cannot attend in person, we can arrange key collection, provided full access and relevant documentation are organized beforehand.

pages.title: Site hour
pages.content:
Every valuation by Kantei Valuers begins with sixty structured minutes on your pavement and inside your building. We measure floor areas, examine physical condition, and verify lease boundaries before opening our evidence files.

00–10 min

The Plan

The site hour begins on the pavement and in the entrance lobby. The property owner or agent unfolds the legal lease plan, and together we walk the perimeter to establish exact property boundaries. We verify all shared corridors, access rights, fire exits, and dedicated loading entrances. This initial ten minutes ensures complete clarity regarding what physical areas are demised to which tenants, identifying any informal annexes, storage basements, or external yard spaces that might differ from registered lease paperwork. Establishing boundaries at the outset prevents costly misunderstandings later in the valuation process.

10–35 min

The Tape

Between ten and thirty-five minutes, our valuer undertakes a comprehensive physical measurement of the property using steel tapes and calibrated laser distance meters. Every individual floor and demised suite is measured to calculate accurate net internal area. For shops and retail units, we measure retail frontage, shop depth, and zone depths in accordance with standard retail valuation practice. For office blocks and industrial units, we measure usable floorplates, stair cores, structural columns, and clear internal eaves heights. These on-site measurements form the quantitative foundation of our valuation and are cross-checked against registered drawings.

35–50 min

The Condition

The third quarter of the site hour focuses on the physical condition and mechanical installations of the building. The valuer inspects external facades, roofing membranes, structural joints, rainwater goods, heating and cooling plant, electrical distribution boards, and fire escapes. We review building accessibility, lift installations, and visible maintenance defects or signs of dampness. Every noteworthy element is photographed with natural lighting to compile a photographic record for the report appendix. While our inspection is not a structural building survey, recording visible repair standards is essential for determining capital allowances, yields, and refurbishment liabilities.

50–60 min

The Documents

The final ten minutes are dedicated to documentation and operational details. The valuer sits with the owner or manager to discuss occupational leases, current rent collection, arrears, unexpired lease terms, service-charge budgets, and upcoming break options. We review running costs, tenant covenant strengths, and any ongoing disputes or planned capital expenditures. Before departing, we agree on any outstanding paperwork needed from the owner's legal advisors and confirm the ten-working-day delivery timeline for your signed twenty-page valuation report.

Before the Hour and After the Hour

A disciplined site inspection requires preparation beforehand and thorough analysis afterwards. Before the hour, Aoife Gallagher confirms the appointment time between 08:00 and 16:00 and gathers preliminary address details, while Tobias Reinholt reviews initial lease documentation. After the site hour concludes, the valuer returns to our Dublin office to process measurement calculations and review photographic evidence. Priya Nair examines our internal transactions database to select recent market comparables, and the valuer drafts the report narrative. Every draft is then audited by Daniel Kowalczyk before formal valuer signature.

Who Should Be There and What to Have Ready

We recommend having the property owner, asset manager, or commercial letting agent present during the site hour. Having an informed representative on site ensures prompt access to plant rooms, risers, and locked tenant units. Please ensure keys, alarm codes, and all relevant lease documents are readily accessible. For larger commercial properties exceeding 5,000 square metres, we automatically schedule a second consecutive hour on site to complete measurements and inspections thoroughly, with no additional fee charged. Site visits are booked Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 16:00.

pages.title: Report
pages.content:
Every commercial property valuation by Kantei Valuers results in a signed, written report of about twenty pages plus photographic appendices. Delivered within ten working days of the site hour, our reports give lenders and owners an unambiguous figure they can rely on.

pp. 1–4

Summary, Instruction and Assumptions

The opening pages of our valuation report provide immediate clarity for credit committees, company directors, and legal advisors. Pages 1 and 2 present the executive summary, stating the market value figure in euros, the formal valuation date, the specific basis of valuation adopted, and the principal valuer's signature line. Pages 3 and 4 detail the precise instruction parameters, identifying the instructing client, the defined purpose of the appraisal whether for loan security, sale, or accounting, and any agreed special assumptions. This structure ensures that any reader immediately understands the figure, its legal context, and the scope of reliance.

pp. 5–10

Property Description and Condition

Pages 5 through 8 deliver a detailed description of the commercial property, detailing its macro location, surrounding transport infrastructure, local commercial environment, and site boundaries. This section itemizes our laser-measured floor dimensions and calculated net internal areas across each floor and demised unit. Pages 9 and 10 record the physical condition observed during our sixty-minute site inspection. Written in plain, direct English without unnecessary technical jargon, this section notes the state of external elevations, roof coverings, mechanical services, fire safety provisions, and visible maintenance requirements, cross-referenced to high-resolution photographs included in the appendices.

pp. 11–17

Tenure, Leases and Market Evidence

The middle section of the report details legal tenure and market dynamics. Pages 11 to 13 analyze occupational lease agreements, reviewing headline rents, passing rents, rent review mechanisms, unexpired terms, break options, and the financial strength of tenant covenants, examined by Tobias Reinholt. Pages 14 to 17 set out verifiable market evidence compiled by Priya Nair from our practice transaction files. We document recent commercial sales and lettings across the immediate locality, detailing transaction dates, achieved capital values, rental rates per square metre, and explaining precisely why each comparable was selected or adjusted.

pp. 18–20

Valuation Methodology and Risks

The concluding pages present the core valuation analysis and risk evaluation. Pages 18 to 20 set out the valuation methodology applied, whether investment capitalization or comparative analysis, showing complete mathematical workings and adopted yields. We highlight specific risks to capital and rental value, including upcoming lease expiries, local vacancy trends, structural maintenance liabilities, and liquidity factors. The section concludes with an index of appendices, which encompass scaled lease and title plans, comprehensive site photographs, and relevant statutory documents, providing a fully transparent, defensible valuation.

Lender Formats and Owner Formats

We tailor the presentation of our twenty-page report to suit the instructing party. For commercial banks and mortgage lenders, we incorporate institutional reporting templates, lender risk scorecards, and specialized security matrices to streamline internal loan underwriting. For property owners, buyers, and corporate sellers, our reports emphasize commercial negotiation insights, market yield trends, lease re-gearing opportunities, and balance-sheet asset figures. In both formats, the fundamental rigor, factual transparency, and independent valuation figures remain identical, audited thoroughly by Daniel Kowalczyk before release.

When the Report Is Late

Our practice commits to delivering every signed valuation report within ten working days of completing the site hour, once all required documents are received. We respect transaction deadlines and banking schedules. If an unforeseen circumstance or delayed document from a third party threatens this timeframe, we tell you the new date the day we know. Clients always receive direct, honest communication from our Dublin office, explaining the reason for any delay and confirming the revised delivery date.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
Kantei Valuers operates on transparent, fixed professional fees confirmed in writing before we step onto your pavement. Our fees are in euros, excluding VAT, and never depend on the valuation figure.

Standard Commercial Fee Schedule

We maintain seven transparent fixed fees for commercial valuation instructions across Ireland, quoted in euros excluding VAT. A shop or retail unit up to 500 square metres is 1,450 euros for a site hour and full report. An office building or single floor up to 2,000 square metres is 2,400 euros. An industrial unit or warehouse up to 5,000 square metres is 2,650 euros. A mixed-use block of up to 12 units is 3,200 euros. For a property portfolio of 2 to 5 properties under one ownership, our fee starts from 2,100 euros per property, including individual site hours and a combined report. A formal lease renewal or rent review opinion is 950 euros for a site hour and letter of opinion. An update of our own valuation report within 12 months is 650 euros as a desk review.

Fee Notes and Inclusions

Four core operating principles govern every quotation issued by Kantei Valuers. First, your fee is fixed in a formal written quotation before the site hour takes place, ensuring complete budget certainty. Second, all travel expenses for properties situated within 150 kilometres of our Dublin office at 27 Merchants Row are fully included without additional travel charges. Third, your professional invoice is issued alongside the signed valuation report and remains payable within thirty days of delivery. Fourth, our fee never depends on the valuation figure. We provide an independent, objective assessment of market value that remains entirely unaffected by transaction outcomes or lending approvals.

Fees for Lenders and Fees for Owners

We maintain identical, equitable pricing structures whether instructed by commercial lenders or directly by property owners. For lender instructions, Aoife Gallagher coordinates directly with institutional credit teams to confirm required loan security templates and issues a fixed fee quote within one working day. For owner instructions, we quote the same published rates for pre-sale advice, purchase appraisals, or annual balance-sheet reporting. By applying uniform, transparent pricing regardless of who instructs, we preserve the professional independence of our valuation opinions and ensure neither lenders nor owners pay arbitrary premiums.

Payment Terms and Cancellation Policy

We understand that commercial transactions evolve. Clients may move a booked site hour free of charge provided notice is given at least one working day prior to the appointment. Site hours can be rebooked on any weekday between 08:00 and 16:00. Invoices are payable within thirty days of receiving your completed report. To maintain strict professional integrity, Kantei Valuers never promises a specific valuation figure, loan approval, or sale price prior to the completion of our site hour and comparables research. Every valuation is an evidence-based professional opinion.

pages.title: Rent Notes
pages.content:
Rent Notes is a quarterly publication from Kantei Valuers delivering a factual record of commercial lettings and sales compared by our practice. The first issue will be published in January 2027.

What an Issue Holds

Rent Notes is designed as a single, printed-style page delivered by email once every quarter. Each issue provides a concise, factual summary of the commercial sales and lease transactions our practice analyzed over the preceding three months across Ireland. Compiled by comparables researcher Priya Nair and lease analyst Tobias Reinholt, the publication describes achieved rents, floor areas, tenant covenants, and transaction dates in clear narrative prose. We present verified evidence of completed deals rather than speculative market forecasts, economic predictions, or promotional commentary, giving readers an objective snapshot of commercial property values.

Who It Is For

Rent Notes is written for commercial property professionals who require grounded market intelligence. It serves commercial lending officers evaluating loan security across retail, office, and industrial sectors; property owners and institutional landlords planning upcoming lease renewals or rent reviews; and commercial buyers assessing prevailing capital values. By focusing strictly on factual transactions within our 150-kilometre coverage area around Dublin, each quarterly issue provides practical context for negotiating lease terms, assessing tenant covenants, and understanding actual market yields without relying on generalized promotional reports.

First Issue: January 2027 and Early Access

The inaugural issue of Rent Notes will be published in January 2027. We are currently accepting registrations for our early-access waitlist. To join, simply submit your name, professional email address, and select your primary role as a lender, property owner, or commercial agent. There is no subscription fee or ongoing obligation. Joining the early-access list ensures you receive the first issue directly in your inbox upon release, accompanied by clean tabular summaries of key commercial lettings and sales analyzed by our Dublin valuation team.

Privacy and Data Handling

Your contact information is treated with strict confidentiality. Kantei Valuers uses your registered details exclusively to distribute quarterly editions of Rent Notes and administrative notices regarding the publication. We never share, sell, or disclose subscriber details to external marketing organizations or third-party agencies. Every email distribution includes an immediate unsubscribe option, allowing you to remove your address from our mailing database at any time. Our subscriber records are held securely at our Dublin office in compliance with Irish data protection legislation.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Request an appraisal or discuss an upcoming commercial property instruction with our Dublin office. Aoife Gallagher will provide a fixed written fee quote within one working day.

Instruct as a Lender or Instruct as an Owner

Initiating an instruction with Kantei Valuers is straightforward whether you are a financial institution or a private owner. When contacting us, provide the property address, the building type, the purpose of the valuation, and your target completion date. Lenders instructing loan security valuations can email our lender desk directly at instruct@kantei.example with any specific reporting requirements. Property owners seeking valuations for sales, purchases, lease renewals, or company accounts can use the same contact point. Aoife Gallagher reviews every request and responds with a fixed written fee quotation within one working day.

Office Location and Contact Details

Our practice is located at 27 Merchants Row, Dublin 2, Ireland. Our office is open Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 17:30 Irish time, during which our administration team is available by telephone at +353 1 000 0611 or via email at instruct@kantei.example. Site hours for physical inspections are booked on weekdays between 08:00 and 16:00. Whether you wish to discuss an upcoming portfolio instruction, deliver property deeds and lease files, or speak directly with our principal valuer Orla Brennan, our Dublin office provides calm and attentive assistance.

What Happens Next

Our instruction workflow follows three reliable steps. First, upon receiving your inquiry with property details, Aoife Gallagher issues a fixed written fee quote within one working day. Second, once you accept the quotation and provide preliminary lease paperwork, we book your sixty-minute site hour between 08:00 and 16:00 on an agreed weekday. Third, our valuer inspects the property, verifies measurements and condition, and delivers your signed twenty-page valuation report within ten working days of the site hour, provided all required tenancy documents have been received.

Coverage Area and Travel Policy

Kantei Valuers undertakes commercial valuations throughout Ireland. For all commercial buildings situated within 150 kilometres of our Dublin office, travel expenses are completely included in our fixed fee, with zero additional travel charges. This primary service territory covers the Greater Dublin Area and regional commercial centers including Drogheda, Dundalk, Naas, and Kilkenny. For properties situated further afield across Ireland, we are pleased to review the asset details and issue a bespoke fee quote covering necessary travel time and site arrangements.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Kantei Valuers respects the confidentiality of clients, building owners, and tenants. This policy outlines how our Dublin practice handles commercial property records, personal details, and valuation files.

Information We Collect and Receive

In providing commercial property valuations, Kantei Valuers collects contact information and detailed property documentation. When you instruct our practice or request a fee quote, we record your name, corporate organization, telephone number, and email address. To prepare our valuation reports, we also receive sensitive commercial records from owners and lenders, including occupational leases, side agreements, tenant rent rolls, service-charge budgets, title plans, and building insurance schedules. All records are processed strictly to fulfill our professional valuation instruction or to respond directly to your legitimate service inquiries.

How We Use and Protect Valuation Data

We treat all client and tenancy information with complete confidentiality. Commercial lease data and physical inspection findings are used exclusively by our nine team members to calculate accurate market values and compile our signed twenty-page valuation reports. Transaction details retained in our practice comparables file by Priya Nair are anonymized for internal benchmarking and quarterly Rent Notes summaries. We never sell, rent, or disclose client information or tenancy details to third-party commercial marketing firms, advertisers, or unauthorized external entities under any circumstances.

Document Security and Data Retention

Valuation files, including signed reports, physical measurement sheets, site photographs, and submitted lease copies, are stored securely within our office systems at 27 Merchants Row, Dublin 2. Access to client records is restricted to authorized practice personnel including our report editor Daniel Kowalczyk and principal valuers. We retain valuation files for standard statutory and professional limitation periods following report delivery, after which digital records and physical papers are securely archived or destroyed. Clients may contact instruct@kantei.example to request details regarding their personal data.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
These terms of business govern all commercial property valuation instructions accepted by Kantei Valuers. We confirm our fixed professional fees in writing before attending the site hour.

Professional Fee Schedule and Notes

All valuation instructions are subject to our fixed professional fee schedule, stated in euros excluding VAT: shop or retail unit up to 500 m² at 1,450 euros; office building or floor up to 2,000 m² at 2,400 euros; industrial unit or warehouse up to 5,000 m² at 2,650 euros; mixed-use block up to 12 units at 3,200 euros; portfolio of 2 to 5 properties from 2,100 euros per property; lease renewal or rent review opinion at 950 euros; and an update of our own report within 12 months at 650 euros. Fees are fixed in writing before the site hour. Travel within 150 km of Dublin is included. Invoices are issued with the signed report, payable in thirty days, and the fee never depends on the valuation figure.

Professional Independence and Advance Figures

Kantei Valuers maintains absolute professional independence on every instruction. We never promise a valuation figure, loan approval, or sale price prior to the completion of our site hour and subsequent evidence analysis. Our professional fee is strictly based on the scope of work and property type, never as a percentage of property value or conditional upon loan drawdown or transaction completion. This policy ensures that our signed valuation report remains an impartial, objective market assessment that lenders and owners can rely on with total confidence.

Site Inspections and Report Delivery Standards

Each valuation instruction includes a sixty-minute physical inspection on site, with an additional second hour provided at no extra charge for commercial buildings exceeding 5,000 square metres. Clients may reschedule a booked site hour free of charge provided notice is given at least one working day before the inspection date. We deliver our signed twenty-page valuation report within ten working days of the site hour, contingent upon receiving all necessary leases, rent rolls, title plans, and planning documents. Where third-party documents are delayed, we notify the client immediately on the day we know.

Property Scope and Jurisdictional Exclusions

Our practice undertakes valuations exclusively for commercial real estate within Ireland. We accept instructions for five property types: retail shops, office buildings, industrial warehouses, mixed-use commercial blocks, and small hotels or leisure properties. We do not provide valuations for private residential homes, speculative development land lacking planning permission, petrol filling stations, specialist trading facilities, or any properties situated outside Ireland. All valuation reports are signed by our qualified valuers and are prepared solely for the instructing client and agreed reliance parties named in the report.

posts.title: A Corner Shop and the Flat Above, Valued for a Refinance
posts.excerpt: How a sixty-minute site inspection in Drogheda uncovered an overlooked lease detail and delivered a signed refinance valuation in eight working days.
posts.content:
Earlier this year, Kantei Valuers received an appraisal request from a commercial lender seeking a loan security valuation for a refinance. The property was a mixed-use commercial building in Drogheda: a ground-floor corner retail shop with a residential flat situated above. The lender required a signed valuation report in their specific credit reporting format to assess loan-to-value ratios before finalizing refinancing terms. Aoife Gallagher at our Dublin instructions desk reviewed the address and property type, issuing a fixed written fee quote within one working day. Upon agreement, our principal valuer Orla Brennan booked the site hour for 08:00 on a Tuesday morning.

The site inspection followed our standard four-part sixty-minute structure. Orla arrived on site within our 150-kilometre complimentary travel radius from our office at 27 Merchants Row, Dublin 2. During the first ten minutes, Orla met the property owner on the pavement to examine the lease plan. As they traced the property boundaries, a critical discrepancy emerged between the owner's recollection and the registered title documents. The building included an enclosed rear yard accessible via a side lane. The owner assumed the yard was vacant and unencumbered, but Orla's review of the title plan and occupational leases revealed that the yard was formally let to a neighbouring tradesperson under an active commercial tenancy with an unexpired term.

Between ten and thirty-five minutes, Orla measured the building using steel tape and laser distance meters to determine net internal areas. She measured retail frontage and shop depth for the ground-floor retail unit, noting the customer trading area and ancillary rear storage. The residential flat above, accessed via a separate side entrance, was measured room by room. From thirty-five to fifty minutes, Orla inspected the building's physical condition, examining the pitched roof, external brick elevations, rainwater gutters, electrical consumer units, and emergency escape routes, capturing high-resolution photographs for the report appendix. The final ten minutes were spent gathering tenancy documentation, including the shop lease, the residential tenancy agreement, the overlooked yard agreement, and the building insurance schedule.

Back at our Dublin office, the valuation process moved into detailed analysis. Tobias Reinholt examined the lease terms, rent review provisions, and tenant covenants across the retail space, residential flat, and rear yard. Priya Nair retrieved verified commercial transaction comparables from our practice file, analyzing recent retail lettings and mixed-use investment sales in Drogheda and surrounding towns. Orla synthesized the physical measurements, condition findings, and market yields to determine the property's market value. Daniel Kowalczyk then audited the twenty-page report, verifying calculations, assumptions, and photographic appendices against the lender's compliance template.

The signed valuation report was delivered to the instructing lender in eight working days from the site hour, well inside our standard ten-working-day commitment. By uncovering the overlooked let yard during the site hour, our valuation provided the lender with an accurate, defensible assessment of passing rent, covenant security, and market value. Our invoice was issued alongside the completed report at the agreed fixed fee of 3,200 euros excluding VAT for a mixed-use block, demonstrating how disciplined on-site observation and thorough lease analysis protect both lender security and owner clarity.

posts.excerpt: One page a quarter, by email. The first issue is in January 2027.
posts.content:
Rent Notes is one printed-style page a quarter, by email: the lettings and sales the practice compared that quarter, described in words and never as a forecast.

The first issue goes out in January 2027. The Rent Notes page is the early-access list.

posts.title: What to send before a site hour
posts.excerpt: Leases and side letters, rent roll, title plan, service-charge budget, insurance schedule and planning permissions.
posts.content:
The site hour goes best when the papers are close at hand. We ask for leases and side letters, the rent roll, the title plan, the service-charge budget, the building insurance schedule and any planning permissions.

Bring the lease plan to the site hour. The rest can follow the same day. The ten working days to the signed report start once the documents are received.
